retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment

  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.

distinct from the intramedullary nailing typically used for shaft fractures. collision as the unrestrained driver of a passenger vehicle that struck a tree at an estimated 60 mph. The patient was ejected from the
vehicle and was found unresponsive at the scene. EMS assessment on arrival documented GCS 8 with tachycardia (HR 130) and

Hospital Course
[[NAME-0019]] presented as a Level 1 trauma activation following a high-speed motor vehicle collision with ejection resulting in
severe polytrauma with hemorrhagic shock. Emergency damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy was performed, followed by IR
embolization of a bleeding right internal iliac branch. The course was complicated by right hemopneumothorax requiring tube
thoracostomy, pelvic ring injury requiring external fixation on ICU day 3, right femoral shaft fracture requiring intramedullary nailing on ICU
day 4, Grade II liver laceration managed non-operatively, rhabdomyolysis with AKI managed with aggressive hydration, hospital-acquired
methicillin-susceptible S. aureus ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefazolin, catheter-associated right common femoral DVT
treated with therapeutic anticoagulation, post-traumatic stress reaction managed with supportive care and psychiatric consultation, and
profound ICU-acquired weakness. Post-splenectomy pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Haemophilus influenzae vaccines were
administered. Extubation was successful on ICU day 9 with brief VAP requiring aggressive pulmonary toileting rather than reintubation.
The patient is transferred to an acute inpatient rehabilitation facility for continued orthopedic and functional recovery with
non-weight-bearing precautions on the right lower extremity.

EDUCATION
Documented teaching with teach-back; per-medication education included
[p.214] Clinician Note: Per-medication education is provided at initiation of each new medication and at discharge. Teach-back is documented
for each session. Learning barriers: critical illness and delirium early in the course; participation improved with recovery. Interpreter not
required (English).
Norepinephrine (Levophed)
Purpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.
Dose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.
Side Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.
Monitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.
Teach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.
Vancomycin
Purpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.
Dose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.
Side Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).
Monitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.
Teach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.
Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)
Purpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.
Dose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.
Side Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).
Monitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.
Teach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.
Pantoprazole (Protonix)
Purpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
Dose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.
Side Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.
Monitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.
Teach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.
Enoxaparin (Lovenox)
Purpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.
Dose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.
Side Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).
[p.409] Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.
Teach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call
for help (unusual bleeding).
Insulin infusion / Sliding scale
Purpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.
Dose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.
Side Effects
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.
Monitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.
Teach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.
Amiodarone
Purpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).
Dose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.
Side Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use
sunscreen.
Monitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.
Teach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials
provided.
Apixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge
Purpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).
Dose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.
Side Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.
Monitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.
Teach-Back Patient and son demonstrated understanding of dose schedule and verbalized to avoid
ibuprofen. Written instruction sheet given.

Patient: [[NAME-0019]]
Date: 2026-12-28
Destination: Acute Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility
Why You Are Being Transferred: You are being transferred to an acute inpatient rehabilitation facility to continue recovery
from your injuries with intensive physical and occupational therapy.
Your Diagnoses (Plain Language)
You were in a serious car accident with multiple injuries. Your spleen was removed and your pelvis and right thigh were fixed with metal
hardware. You had a blood clot in your leg and a lung infection which are being treated. With rehabilitation you will continue to improve.
Medicines
Take all medications as prescribed including antibiotics, blood thinner for the leg clot, pain medications, and a medication for
anxiety/stress. Do not stop the blood thinner without your doctor's instruction.
Activity
Participate fully in physical and occupational therapy. Follow non-weight-bearing precautions on your right leg. Use your walker as
prescribed. Follow pelvic precautions to allow healing.
Diet & Feeding
Eat a well-balanced diet with adequate protein for healing. Drink plenty of fluids.
Devices, Lines & Wounds
Your pelvic external fixator will remain in place until removal by orthopedic surgery. Keep pin sites clean and dry. Watch for redness,
drainage, or pain at pin sites.
Equipment / Supplies Arranged
Walker for non-weight-bearing ambulation, pin-site care supplies, wound care supplies, and medical alert bracelet for post-splenectomy
status - coordinated with the rehabilitation facility.
Follow-Up Appointments
Specialty | When | Purpose
Trauma Surgery | 2-4 weeks | Post-injury follow-up
Orthopedic Surgery | 2 weeks | Hardware and fracture healing
Physiatry / Rehabilitation | Per rehab | Ongoing rehabilitation
Infectious Diseases | Per rehab | Complete antibiotic course
Hematology / Anticoagulation | 1-2 weeks | DVT management
Psychiatry | 2-4 weeks | Post-traumatic stress follow-up
Primary Care | After rehab | General health and immunizations
When to Get Help Immediately
Call for help right away for: fever, breathing difficulty, wound drainage or opening, hardware pain or infection at pin sites, leg swelling or
pain, chest pain, bleeding, or worsening symptoms of anxiety or depression.

judge_messages.content:
You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Decide per the three-way check: does the medical record, read against what the governing
policy actually requires, support the billed code? Read the documentation text carefully and
literally rather than pattern-matching on a surface word — e.g. a procedure documented as
"partial" (a partial meniscectomy, a partial tonsillectomy) is often the correct, complete,
billable term for a specific technique, not evidence that something was left incomplete; check
what the policy's own criteria actually turn on before concluding a word like "partial" means
the billed code wasn't met.

Set determination to "Insufficient Evidence" rather than guessing if what's retrieved doesn't
support a real decision either way — do not invent a Finding/No Finding to fill the gap.

system_note is the auditor note a human reviewer reads on EVERY claim, Finding or not — write
it with explicit citations (document/section/page) and reasoning a reviewer could audit line by
line; a correct determination with a
vague, citation-free note still scores as a weak note (see the quality bar in the schema
field's own description).

rationale_letter is a SEPARATE, formal appeal-ready letter to the provider — only written when
determination is Finding (null otherwise). It restates the finding and its basis for an
external, non-technical reader, not a repeat of system_note's internal auditor reasoning.

Page numbers: a medical-record note can span several PDF pages, and its page_start/page_end
are not the page of any particular line in it. In a long note's text, a [p.N] marker means the
text after it (up to the next marker) is on physical page N; cite that page in system_note,
never a note's page_start/page_end range. A note whose page_start equals its page_end is all on
that page. In a multi-page note with no marker before the line, name the note without a page.

evidence_cited must reference only passages that actually appear in the retrieved rows above.
Each entry is the source_id of the one row the quote comes from, copied exactly, and the quote
copied verbatim from that row's text, character for character: don't wrap part of it in
quotation marks, fix a typo, or drop a word or code from the middle. Never invent or recall one. Code checks each quote
against that row and fills in the document, section and page from it, so a quote that isn't in
the cited row, or a source_id that wasn't retrieved, is dropped. Each quote is ONE contiguous
passage from a single row: if you need two separate passages, give two separate evidence_cited
entries rather than joining them with "..."; a stitched-together quote can't be verified. Rows
with no source_id (claim lines, code descriptions, a tool's own summary rows) aren't citable;
cite the record or policy row behind them instead.

Patient name, MRN, and date of birth appear as de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] —
including inline inside quoted note/fact text — not real values. Reproduce them exactly as
given in system_note, rationale_letter, and evidence_cited quotes; a separate step restores
the real values afterward. Never remark on the token format or guess/reconstruct what it stands
for.

discharge_disposition, finding_reason, recovery_type, skilled_services,
adjusted_date_of_service, corrected_revenue_code, adjusted_units_billed,
revised_diagnosis_set, and revised_procedure_set are only meaningful for specific review types
(DRG, Readmission, SNF, SNF, SNF, SNF, DRG, and DRG respectively) — see each field's own schema
description and this review type's domain notes above to know whether to populate it; leave it
null when this review type doesn't call for it.

If this is a DRG review: you are deciding for the WHOLE claim in one pass, not one line — check
every diagnosis and procedure line given to you (POA, CC/MCC tier, whether it's still
supported), not just the one the question happens to name first. revised_diagnosis_set and
revised_procedure_set must each be the claim's COMPLETE corrected list (every code that should
remain billed, in the same shape as what you were given, position 1 = principal diagnosis) —
not a delta of only the line(s) that changed. code_decisions is what's scored: one entry per
billed code, each exactly once, plus additions, with the POA and CC/MCC tier each diagnosis
should carry, and the evidence_cited IDs behind every change. Code checks it and builds the
corrected lists from it.

result.system_note: MR_20 - DRG three-way check (claim vs. medical record vs. policy). Summary of changes: remove R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) and S06.2X9A (traumatic subdural hemorrhage); change POA for N17.9 (acute kidney failure) from N to Y; change severity tier for J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia) to MCC (policy). Rationale, evidence, and policy citations below. What was billed (examples): principal diagnosis S36.032A (Major laceration of spleen, POA=Y, MCC); other major billed lines included S72.301A (right femoral shaft fracture, MCC), T79.4XXA (traumatic shock, MCC), N17.9 (AKI, billed POA=N, CC), J95.851 (VAP, billed CC/POA=N). See full billed list in code_decisions/revised_diagnosis_set. Evidence from the medical record (key passages): - Splenic injury / operative management: CT panscan demonstrates Grade IV splenic laceration with active extravasation (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13, p.448) and the admission H&P documents transfer to the OR for damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy and IR embolization for pelvic bleeding (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9, p.849). Evidence: ev3, ev2; policy: S36.032A is AAST Grade III-V (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Splenic-Injury.docx-b8) (ev10). These satisfy the splenic-injury validation criteria for S36.032A (MCC) and support keeping it as principal (position 1). Evidence cited: ev3 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13) and ev2 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9) and ev10 (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Splenic-Injury.docx-b8). - Right femur fracture, pelvic injury, chest injury: CT panscan and orthopedic consult document displaced mid-shaft right femur fracture and pelvic ring disruption and right hemopneumothorax with multiple right rib fractures; operative external fixation and subsequent intramedullary nailing are documented (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13 p.448; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n25 p.48; discharge summary). Evidence: ev3, ev4, orthopedics consult n25. Evidence cited: ev3 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13) and ev4 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13). - Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP): Infectious Diseases documents "VAP developing shortly after extubation with clinical and radiographic features" and portable CXR reads new right lower-lobe consolidation (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n70, p.963). Discharge summary explicitly documents "hospital-acquired methicillin-susceptible S. aureus ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefazolin" and notes resolution (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n1247, p.1093). Policy: J95.851 is a VAP code that carries MCC and requires provider documentation of VAP with appropriate timing and clinical/radiographic criteria; policy also requires POA = N for VAP by definition (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8 / -b73) (ev11). The clinical documentation (ID consult + discharge summary) meets the policy criteria for VAP (onset in hospital, radiographic/new infiltrate, clinical criteria, and organism identified), so J95.851 should be supported and should carry MCC. Evidence cited: ev6 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n70), ev5 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n1247), ev11 (policy RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8). - Acute kidney injury (N17.9) POA timing: The admission History & Physical (admitting H&P) lists "7 | Rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis-requiring" on the active problem list of the admission note (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9, p.849). This is provider documentation of AKI on the admission H&P, supporting that AKI was present on admission (POA = Y). Policy for N17.9 requires provider documentation and KDIGO objective data or initiation of RRT; the record contains provider AKI documentation and subsequent creatinine elevations consistent with KDIGO staging (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b8) (ev12). Therefore POA should be Y for N17.9. Evidence cited: ev9 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9) and ev12 (policy RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b8). - Unsupported billed diagnoses (removed): - R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) - billed but unsupported: the record documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock (EMS/hospital vitals: hypotension SBP 78 on arrival; H&P and Plan explicitly address hemorrhagic shock with massive transfusion protocol and damage-control laparotomy/IR embolization) rather than cardiogenic shock. There is no documentation of a cardiac cause for shock (no cardiology/ischemia/ventricular failure documentation). The admission H&P documents hypotension and MTP activation (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9, p.849) consistent with hemorrhagic/traumatic shock; cardiogenic shock is not supported and should be removed. Evidence cited: ev8 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9) - contradicts R57.01. - S06.2X9A (traumatic subdural hemorrhage) - billed as traumatic subdural with LOC; CT trauma panscan shows "Head: no acute intracranial hemorrhage; mild scalp hematoma." (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13, p.448). There is no radiographic or operative documentation of an acute subdural hemorrhage. Remove S06.2X9A. Evidence cited: ev7 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13) - contradicts S06.2X9A. Policy references used for key checks: - Splenic injury code validation: S36.032A requires AAST Grade III-V documentation or operative/procedural equivalence; operative splenectomy or CT Grade IV meets the policy for S36.032A (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Splenic-Injury.docx-b8) (ev10). - VAP: J95.851 is an MCC-level VAP code and requires documented provider VAP diagnosis with timing (>48 hours after intubation or otherwise hospital-acquired), radiographic/infectious evidence, and appropriate antibiotic management; policy also requires POA = N for VAP (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8) (ev11). - AKI: N17.9 requires explicit provider documentation of AKI plus KDIGO criteria or initiation of RRT; admission H&P documents AKI on admission (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b8) (ev12). Action taken (how the claim is corrected): - Removed diagnosis codes unsupported by the record: R57.01 and S06.2X9A (see evidence ev8, ev7). - Retained S36.032A as principal diagnosis (supported by CT and operative splenectomy; policy confirms MCC status for Grade III-V splenic laceration) (ev3, ev2, ev10). - Corrected POA for N17.9 to Y because the admission H&P documents AKI on admission (ev9, ev12). - Upgraded J95.851 to MCC severity per the governing VAP policy and documented ID/discharge notes confirming hospital-acquired VAP with organism and treatment (ev6, ev5, ev11). Revised diagnosis list (complete, position 1 = principal) after audit corrections: [S36.032A, S72.301A, S32.810A, S22.42XA, S27.4XXA, S36.115A, T79.4XXA, M62.88, N17.9, J95.851, B95.62, I82.401, F43.10, D62, Z87.891, Z90.81]. Rationale: removed codes without clinical/radiographic support (R57.01, S06.2X9A); other codes retained with corrected POA/severity where applicable. Revised procedure list (complete): [0BH17EZ, 07TP0ZZ, 0WH30YZ, 04L33DZ, 0SH90BZ, 0QH60BZ, 0QQ606Z, 30233N1, 02HV33Z, 5A1D90Z]. These are supported by the admission H&P, imaging, operative and discharge documentation (ev2, ev3, ev4, ev5). Disposition documented in the record: Transfer: Acute Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (see Transfer Instructions / Discharge Summary NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n1243 / n1247, p.1091-1093). If you want, I can (a) assemble a provider-facing audit rationale letter for appeal (I have prepared one below), and (b) produce a delta-only report enumerating every line that changed vs. the original claim. Evidence citations: ev1-ev12 below list the exact passages relied on (document/section/page included in each source_id).
result.rationale_letter: To: Coding/Health Information Management and Trauma Surgery Department From: Senior Clinical Claims Auditor Re: MR_20 - DRG audit of inpatient stay (level 1 trauma activation), admission 2026-08-03 We reviewed the documentation, billed diagnoses/procedures, and the governing DRG coding policies for the above inpatient encounter. Based on a three-way check (claim lines vs. the medical record vs. governing condition policies), we have the following Finding(s) that require correction to the submitted claim coding. Finding summary (changes being made): 1) R57.01 (Cardiogenic shock) - REMOVED. Basis: The medical record documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock with hypotension on arrival (SBP 78), massive transfusion protocol activation, and damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy/IR embolization for hemorrhage control (History & Physical, 2026-08-03; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9; CT trauma panscan NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13). There is no documentation of a cardiogenic etiology (no cardiac ischemia, depressed ventricular function, or cardiology assessment supporting cardiogenic shock). Claim assignment of cardiogenic shock is not supported by the clinical record and is therefore removed (evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9, p.849 - EMS/hospital hypotension and MTP; ev8). 2) S06.2X9A (Traumatic subdural hemorrhage with LOC) - REMOVED. Basis: The CT trauma panscan explicitly documents "Head: no acute intracranial hemorrhage; mild scalp hematoma." (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13, p.448). There is no radiographic or operative documentation of a subdural hemorrhage; thus S06.2X9A is not supported by the record and is removed (ev7). 3) N17.9 (Acute kidney failure, unspecified) - POA FLAG CORRECTED to Y. Basis: The admission History & Physical lists "Rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis-requiring" on the admission problem list (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9, p.849), indicating provider recognition of AKI on admission. Per the AKI policy (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b8), provider documentation of AKI with KDIGO evidence supports N17.9; therefore the POA indicator should be Y (ev9, ev12). 4) J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia) - SEVERITY CORRECTED to MCC. Basis: Infectious Diseases documents "VAP developing shortly after extubation with clinical and radiographic features" with new CXR consolidation; discharge summary documents hospital-acquired MSSA VAP treated with cefazolin and resolution (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n70 and NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n1247). Governing policy names J95.851 as the VAP code carrying MCC and requires hospital-onset timing and provider-confirmed diagnosis; the documentation meets those criteria and supports MCC (ev6, ev5, ev11). Codes retained as billed (examples): S36.032A (Major splenic laceration) remains principal - CT shows Grade IV splenic laceration with active extravasation and the operative course documents emergent splenectomy (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13 and n9). Right femoral shaft fracture (S72.301A) and pelvic ring injury (S32.810A) are supported by imaging and operative/orthopedic documentation; procedures billed for splenectomy, pelvic external fixation and IM nailing, chest tube, and >96 hours mechanical ventilation are supported by the operative/ICU/discharge notes (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n13, n25, n1247, n9). Policy citations: S36.032A validation (AAST Grade III-V) is met by CT and operative documentation (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Splenic-Injury.docx-b8) (ev10). Corrective action taken on the claim (summary): - Removed R57.01 and S06.2X9A. - Corrected N17.9 POA indicator to Y. - Corrected J95.851 severity to MCC (policy-consistent). - Retained all other billed diagnoses and procedures after verification of supporting documentation and policy alignment (revised diagnosis and procedure lists provided). If you disagree with these specific corrections, please provide the precise clinical documentation that establishes a cardiogenic etiology for shock (e.g., echocardiogram showing new severe ventricular dysfunction, cardiology consult diagnosing cardiogenic shock), or radiographic/operative documentation of an acute subdural hemorrhage, or evidence that AKI first developed after admission rather than being present on arrival. For the VAP severity tier, provide any provider statement or documentation that the pneumonia was present on admission or that the event did not meet VAP timing/clinical criteria. Absent such documentation, the corrections above will stand. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor (References: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n9; -n13; -n70; -n1247; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Splenic-Injury.docx-b8; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b8.)

[NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_20.pdf-n1247] Discharge / Transfer Summary:
Discharge / Transfer Summary
Attending: Dr. Julia Ostrowski, MD (Critical Care Medicine)
Admit: 2026-08-03 Transfer: 2026-12-28
LOS: 147 days
Reason for Admission: Severe polytrauma with hemorrhagic shock following motor vehicle collision.
Admission Diagnoses
Multi-system trauma with hemorrhagic shock following MVC
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolving polytrauma from MVC; status post splenectomy; status post pelvic external fixation; status post right femoral intramedullary
nailing; resolved right hemopneumothorax; resolved MSSA VAP; right femoral DVT on anticoagulation; resolved rhabdomyolysis and
AKI; post-splenectomy immunocompromise; ICU-acquired weakness; post-traumatic stress reaction.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0019]] presented as a Level 1 trauma activation following a high-speed motor vehicle collision with ejection resulting in
severe polytrauma with hemorrhagic shock. Emergency damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy was performed, followed by IR
embolization of a bleeding right internal iliac branch. The course was complicated by right hemopneumothorax requiring tube
thoracostomy, pelvic ring injury requiring external fixation on ICU day 3, right femoral shaft fracture requiring intramedullary nailing on ICU
day 4, Grade II liver laceration managed non-operatively, rhabdomyolysis with AKI managed with aggressive hydration, hospital-acquired
methicillin-susceptible S. aureus ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefazolin, catheter-associated right common femoral DVT
treated with therapeutic anticoagulation, post-traumatic stress reaction managed with supportive care and psychiatric consultation, and
profound ICU-acquired weakness. Post-splenectomy pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Haemophilus influenzae vaccines were
administered. Extubation was successful on ICU day 9 with brief VAP requiring aggressive pulmonary toileting rather than reintubation.
The patient is transferred to an acute inpatient rehabilitation facility for continued orthopedic and functional recovery with
non-weight-bearing precautions on the right lower extremity.
Physical Examination
Vitals: Tmax 37.2°C | HR 79 | MAP 76 | RR 15 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: room air, ambulatory oxygenation preserved. General:
Alert, interactive, comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and
rhythm; no murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft,
non-distended, +bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative;
strength improving with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance. Extremities: ex-fix in place; healing
incisions; non-weight-bearing right leg.
Laboratory Data (Pertinent)
CBC: WBC 7.2 x103/uL, Hgb 9.8 g/dL, Hct 29%, platelets 233 x109/L (neutrophils 75%). BMP: Na 139, K 4.1, Cl 101, CO2 24, BUN 20,
creatinine 1.09 mg/dL, glucose 155 mg/dL, Ca 8.5, Mg 2.2, Phos 3.5. ABG (07:00): pH 7.37 / PaCO2 41 / PaO2 83 / HCO3 21; lactate
1.4 mmol/L; P/F ratio 313.
Imaging (Pertinent)
No new imaging obtained today. Most recent radiograph reviewed and compared; findings consistent with the documented clinical
trajectory.
Condition & Functional Status at Transfer
Alert, oriented, and interactive. Room air with adequate oxygenation. Ambulating with walker and non-weight-bearing precautions on right
lower extremity. Tolerating oral diet with good intake. Hemodynamically stable. Pelvic external fixator in place. Multiple healing incisions.
Transfer Medications
Medication | Dose | Route | Frequency | Indication
Cefazolin | 2 g | IV | q8h (finish course) | MSSA VAP
Apixaban | 5 mg | PO | BID | Right femoral DVT
Sertraline | 25 mg | PO | Daily | Post-traumatic stress
Acetaminophen | 1000 mg | PO | q6h scheduled | Pain control
Oxycodone | 5-10 mg | PO | q4h PRN | Breakthrough pain
Gabapentin | 300 mg | PO | TID | Neuropathic pain
Pantoprazole | 40 mg | PO | Daily | Stress ulcer prophylaxis
Docusate | 100 mg | PO | BID | Constipation prophylaxis
Multivitamin | 1 tab | PO | Daily | Recovery
Follow-Up & Recommendations
1. Continue acute inpatient rehabilitation with intensive PT/OT.
2. Trauma Surgery follow-up in 2-4 weeks.
3. Orthopedic Surgery follow-up at 2 weeks for hardware assessment; non-weight-bearing precautions on right lower extremity for 6
weeks minimum.
4. Complete MSSA VAP antibiotic course.
5. Continue anticoagulation for DVT; hematology follow-up.
6. Primary care follow-up for overall recovery.
7. Psychiatry follow-up for post-traumatic stress.
8. Post-splenectomy precautions: emergency antibiotics for febrile illness, annual vaccinations, medical alert bracelet.
9. Return precautions: fever, respiratory decompensation, worsening leg swelling, bleeding, hardware pain or drainage.

Selection and sequencing of MRSA codes
(a) Combination codes for MRSA infection
When a patient is diagnosed with an infection that is due to
methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), and that
infection has a combination code that includes the causal
organism (e.g., sepsis, pneumonia) assign the appropriate
combination code for the condition (e.g., code A41.02, Sepsis
due to Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus or code
J15.212, Pneumonia due to Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus
aureus). Do not assign code B95.62, Methicillin resistant
Staphylococcus aureus infection as the cause of diseases
classified elsewhere, as an additional code, because the
combination code includes the type of infection and the MRSA
organism. Do not assign a code from subcategory Z16.11,
Resistance to penicillins, as an additional diagnosis.
See Section C.1. for instructions on coding and sequencing of
sepsis and severe sepsis.
(b) Other codes for MRSA infection
When there is documentation of a current infection (e.g., wound
infection, stitch abscess, urinary tract infection) due to MRSA, and
that infection does not have a combination code that includes the
causal organism, assign the appropriate code to identify the
condition along with code B95.62, Methicillin resistant
Staphylococcus aureus infection as the cause of diseases classified
elsewhere for the MRSA infection. Do not assign a code from
subcategory Z16.11, Resistance to penicillins.

[DOC-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx › Coding Considerations › Mutually Exclusive Codes]
A41.02 (Sepsis due to MRSA) and B95.62 (MRSA as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere) cannot be reported together for MRSA sepsis. B95.62 is an etiology code used with site-specific infection codes (e.g., pneumonia, wound infection) — it is not additionally reported when A41.02 is the principal code because the organism is already embedded in A41.02. Reporting both inflates code count and creates audit risk. Auditors should also flag simultaneous use of A41.9 (unspecified organism) and any organism-specific code (A40.-, A41.01–A41.59) for the same episode — these are mutually exclusive.

[DOC-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx › Definitions › MRSA Sepsis vs. MRSA Infection]
MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) sepsis is coded to A41.02 when the provider documents MRSA as the causative organism of sepsis — either by blood culture positivity, by clinical judgment with MRSA from another site driving empiric therapy, or by explicit provider linkage. When MRSA causes a localized infection (e.g., wound infection, pneumonia) without systemic sepsis, the site-specific infection code is used with B95.62 (MRSA as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere) as an additional code. Auditors must confirm whether the provider has characterized the presentation as sepsis vs. localized MRSA infection, as the distinction determines code selection.
